title: IMPLEMENTATION OF RASHTRIYA GRAM SWARAJ ABHIYAN (RGSA) IN WEST BENGAL
body_text:
Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a State subject and part of the State list of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. However, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) since the financial year 2022-23 in States/ UTs. The main objective of the scheme is to strengthen the capacity of Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) by imparting training to Elected Representatives (ERs), Panchayat Functionaries and other stakeholders to develop their governance capabilities for leadership roles, enabling the Gram Panchayats and Local bodies to function effectively across all States/UTs including the State of West Bengal.
Apart from different trainings, the Scheme also supports development of Panchayat infrastructure like Gram Panchayat Bhawan, Computer and Co-location (on a limited scale) of Common Service Centers (CSCs) in Gram Panchayat Bhawan to the States/ UTs including in the State of West Bengal.
Under Revamped RGSA, the Central Empowered Committee of RGSA accords approval to the units under various components based on the Annual Action Plan (AAP) submitted by the State/UT. During the last four years (FY 2022-23 to FY 2025-26), an amount of Rs.130.65 crore was released as Central Share to the State of West Bengal under the Scheme. Out of which, Rs.268.26 crore has been utilized by the State. Utilization of funds includes Central Share, State Share and unspent balance from previous years.
A total of 5,17,632 elected representatives of the State of West Bengal were trained on various aspects on rural governance from FY 2022-23 to FY 2025-26. In addition, 199 units for the construction of Panchayat Bhawans and 1,712 units of Computers were approved under the scheme from FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26. The State has reported that 124 Panchayat Bhawan have been constructed and 1,185 units of computers have been procured during FY 2023-24 to 2026-27 (as on 5 th August 2026).
The State has also reported that all stakeholders of Panchayati Raj Institutions are invited to participate in various training programmes conducted under the Scheme.
Revamped RGSA is demand-driven in nature. Funds are released to States/UTs based on the Annual Action Plans approved by the Central Empowered Committee (CEC), the pace of expenditure by the State and submission of requisite document for release of funds. The funds are utilized only for the approved components as prioritized by the States/UTs. The Ministry releases the funds under the scheme to States/UTs only. Rs.8.00 crore as Central Share in the 1 st Instalment was released to the State of West Bengal in the FY 2026-27 (as on 10 th July 2026).
As informed by the State, 199 units of the construction of Gram Panchayat Bhawans have been approved from FY 2023-24 to 2025-26 under the scheme of Revamped RGSA, out of which 124 units have been completed till 5 th August 2026 and remaining 75 units are different stages of completion. As per the information submitted in the Annual Action Plan of RGSA in the FY 2025-26 by the State, only 87 Gram Panchayats out of 3,339 do not have own building. Under Revamped RGSA Scheme, component wise fund has not been released to the States/UTs. State/UTs utilized the funds based on the approved components of their AAPs as per the priority.
To promote e-enablement of Panchayats, the Ministry is implementing the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP), which has strengthened transparency, efficiency and governance at the grassroots level. As per the information available on Government e Marketplace (GeM) Portal, 267 Panchayats have adopted/ on-boarded on GeM. 1,881 Gram Panchayats have uploaded their Gram Panchayat Development Plan on eGramSwaraj Portal for the Plan Year 2026-27 in the State of West Bengal as on 06.08.2026. As informed by the State Govt. of West Bengal, a total of 10,111 elected representatives have been trained as on date under the scheme in FY 2026-27.
This information was given by Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha on 12 th August 2026.

enrichment.summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply on 12 August 2026, Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) detailed the implementation of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) in West Bengal since FY 2022-23. Rs.130.65 crore was released as Central Share over four years, 5,17,632 elected representatives were trained, 199 Panchayat Bhawan units and 1,712 computer units were approved, with 124 Bhawans and 1,185 computers completed so far. The reply also noted progress under the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project, including GeM onboarding and GPDP uploads on the eGramSwaraj portal.
enrichment.context:
RGSA is the Ministry of Panchayati Raj's flagship capacity-building scheme for Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), running since 2018 and revamped from FY 2022-23, aimed at strengthening grassroots democracy envisaged under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment. Since Panchayats fall under the State List (Entry 5, Seventh Schedule), the Centre's role is largely facilitative and demand-driven, with funds released against State-submitted Annual Action Plans (AAPs) rather than being scheme/component-specific. This reflects the cooperative federalism model in local governance, where the Centre incentivizes reforms (training, infrastructure, e-governance) while implementation authority rests with States.

The reply also highlights the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project, part of the Digital India initiative, which uses platforms like eGramSwaraj (for Gram Panchayat Development Plans) and integration with the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) to enhance transparency and reduce leakages in local government procurement and planning. Such digitization efforts are significant for exam purposes as they intersect with e-governance reforms, decentralization, and Panchayati Raj strengthening—recurring themes in GS Paper 2.

prelims_questions.question: The Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), a Centrally Sponsored Scheme mentioned in the context of Panchayati Raj strengthening, is implemented by which of the following?
options: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that the Ministry of Panchayati Raj implements the Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) since FY 2022-23.

prelims_questions.question: Panchayats, as 'Local Self Government', fall under which List of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release clarifies that Panchayat, being 'Local Self Government', is a State subject and part of the State List of the Seventh Schedule.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) in strengthening Panchayati Raj Institutions. Examine the challenges in implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for a subject that falls under the State List.
